A_target.statement:
Let $\struct {\family {A_i}_{i \mathop \in I}, \family {f_{i j} } }$ be a [[Definition:Directed System|directed system]] of sets.
Then [[Definition:Mapping|mappings]] out of the [[Definition:Direct Limit|direct limit]] correspond to compatible families:
:$\map {\operatorname {Hom} } {\varinjlim A_i, Z} \cong \set {\family {g_i: A_i \to Z}: g_j \circ f_{i j} = g_i}$

B_source.statement:
Let $\sim$ be an [[Definition:Equivalence Relation|equivalence relation]] on a [[Definition:Disjoint Union (Set Theory)|disjoint union]] $\coprod_i A_i$.
Then mappings $\paren {\coprod_i A_i} / \sim \to Z$ correspond to families $g_i: A_i \to Z$ agreeing on identified points.

substitutions.the disjoint union being collapsed: the disjoint union of all terms of the directed system
substitutions.the identifications imposed: an element is identified with each of its images further along the system
substitutions.the quotient object: the direct limit of the system

derived.families of maps agreeing on identificat: families commuting with the transition maps
derived.the induced map out of the quotient: the unique map out of the direct limit

object_map.reformulation: Build the limit as a disjoint union collapsed by the identifications the transition maps impose.

validity_conditions: Directedness makes the identification relation transitive: any two elements have images that eventually land in a common term, where they can be compared.
Compatibility of a family with the transition maps is exactly agreement on the identified pairs, which is the condition for descending to the quotient.
Without directedness the relation generated by the identifications is larger than the relation itself, and the elementwise description of the limit fails.
proof_plan: Form the [[Definition:Disjoint Union (Set Theory)|disjoint union]] $\displaystyle \coprod_{i \mathop \in I} A_i$.

For $a \in A_i$, identify $a$ with $\map {f_{i j} } a \in A_j$ for every $j \ge i$.
Define $a \sim b$ for $a \in A_i$, $b \in A_j$ {{iff}} $\map {f_{i k} } a = \map {f_{j k} } b$ for some $k \ge i, j$.

[[Definition:Reflexive Relation|Reflexivity]] and [[Definition:Symmetric Relation|symmetry]] are immediate.
For [[Definition:Transitive Relation|transitivity]], use that $I$ is [[Definition:Directed Set|directed]] to find a common upper bound, and push both equalities forward.
